text.ja: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS · PROBLEM 1次元Poisson・Dirichlet製造解 この問題の式、参照の条件、計算法、公開済みのコードをたどります。 保存数値データを図示 保存済み1次元Dirichlet製造解の誤差と格子数。 方程式・問題の定義 無次元区間[0,1]で −uₓₓ=π²sin(πx)、u(0)=u(1)=0。中間層16素子・49実パラメータ、固定seed 8401–8403、学習64点と独立評価257点を用います。 Poisson・Laplace方程式 −∇2u=f f=0⟹∇2u=0 楕円型境界値問題。符号規約を確認し、反復解法・疎行列・境界条件をたどる。 実行例で使う式 共通実行例問題の式 1次元Poisson：Dirichlet正弦解と2次収束 −u′′(x)=π2sin⁡(πx),u(0)=u(1)=0 uref(x)=sin⁡(πx) 一様格子の3点差分を15/31/63内部点で解く。残差が小さいことと連続解に近いことは別々に判定する。 補助実行例実行例の定義・検証式 1D Poisson PINNと独立格子誤差 −uxx=π2sin⁡(πx),0<x<1,u(0)=u(1)=0 uθ(x)=x(1−x)[b0+∑j=116ajtanh⁡(wjx+bj)] ri=−uθ,xx(xi)−π2sin⁡(πxi)π2,L=164∑i=164ri2 3固定seedの49パラメータPINNを解析解・FDと比較します。 厳密解・参照解 零Dirichlet境界の製造正弦解、複合正弦の比較例、および離散残差で確認します。単一sin(πx)の参照カードが全ソース条件を表すわけではありません。 全49列の残差Jacobianと損失勾配、空間微分を別資格段階で独立照合。解析解sin(πx)に対する独立点誤差、PDE残差、境界値、FD誤差を別に保存します。収束・精度目標の実際の真偽を残し、正常な予算終了を収束と呼びません。 製造解関連モデルの参照 Poisson／正弦波の製造解 u = sin(πx); −u_xx = f = π² sin(πx) 両端はゼロDirichlet条件。目標解から外力を選ぶ製造解であり、任意の外力のPoisson解ではありません。 単一sin(πx)の共通固定入力とは一致しますが、保存比較図は複合正弦製造解も含みます。同じ零Dirichletでも全ソースが同一ではありません。 製造解関連モデルの参照 1D Poisson PINNと独立格子誤差 u_{\rm exact}(x)=\sin(\pi x);\quad -u_{xx}=\pi^2\sin(\pi x),\quad 0<x<1,\quad u(0)=u(1)=0;\quad u_\theta(x)=x(1-x)\left[b_0+\sum_{j=1}^{16}a_j\tanh(w_jx+b_j)\right];\quad r_i=\frac{-u_{\theta,xx}(x_i)-\pi^2\sin(\pi x_i)}{\pi^2},\quad L=\frac1{64}\sum_{i=1}^{64}r_i^2 無次元区間[0,1]で −uₓₓ=π²sin(πx)、u(0)=u(1)=0。中間層16素子・49実パラメータ、固定seed 8401–8403、学習64点と独立評価257点を用います。 1つの滑らかなPoisson問題と3seedの固定予算実験です。小さい学習損失だけで独立点精度の達成や一般的なPINN学習成功を保証しません。未達目標も表示します。 実行例の参照と結果 共通実行例 1次元Poisson：Dirichlet正弦解と2次収束 CSVは最細格子でx・数値解・解析解・誤差を整列。全3格子の誤差と残差、隣接格子間の次数はresult.jsonに保存。Thomasの原報告は既存台帳でも直接確認未済のため、未検証の一次文献を新たに掲げない。 この問題への対応が共通の固定入力・実行例で明示された手法です。図と実行例の条件の違いは入力で確認してください。 x(1−x)を掛けて境界値を厳密に組み込むtanhネットワークを、解析的な全パラメータJacobian付きTRF最小二乗法で学習します。固定予算後の全モデルを保存し、31/63/127未知数の2次中心差分とThomas法も計算します。 この問題の実行例で使う手法 Plot of saved numerical data Stored error versus resolution for the 1D Dirichlet manufactured solution. Equations and problem definitions Solve dimensionless −uₓₓ=π² sin(πx) on [0,1] with zero Dirichlet data. Use sixteen hidden units, 49 real parameters, seeds 8401–8403, 64 training points and 257 separate evaluation points. Poisson / Laplace equations −∇2u=f f=0⟹∇2u=0 Elliptic boundary-value problems: check sign conventions, iterative solvers, sparse matrices and boundaries. Formulations used by execution examples Common execution exampleProblem definition 1D Poisson: Dirichlet sine solution and second-order refinement −u′′(x)=π2sin⁡(πx),u(0)=u(1)=0 uref(x)=sin⁡(πx) Three-point differences on 15/31/63 uniform interior nodes; a small residual and proximity to the continuous solution are separate checks. Supplementary execution exampleExample definition or validation formula Poisson PINN: independent grid error −uxx=π2sin⁡(πx),0<x<1,u(0)=u(1)=0 uθ(x)=x(1−x)[b0+∑j=116ajtanh⁡(wjx+bj)] ri=−uθ,xx(xi)−π2sin⁡(πxi)π2,L=164∑i=164ri2 Compare a 49-parameter PINN for three fixed seeds with analytic and finite-difference solutions. Exact and reference solutions Use manufactured sine solutions, the composite-sine comparison and discrete residuals with zero Dirichlet endpoints. The single sin(πx) reference does not represent every forcing variant. Independently qualify all 49 residual-Jacobian columns, loss-gradient coordinates and spatial derivatives. Save off-training solution error against sin(πx), PDE residual, boundary error and finite-difference error separately. Preserve actual convergence and accuracy decisions; a normal budget return is not convergence. Manufactured solutionRelated-model reference Poisson / manufactured sine u = sin(πx); −u_xx = f = π² sin(πx) Zero Dirichlet endpoints. The forcing is chosen from the target solution; this is not an arbitrary-source Poisson solution. It matches the single-sine common fixed input, but saved comparisons also contain composite-sine manufactured forcing. Zero Dirichlet boundaries do not make all sources identical. Manufactured solutionRelated-model reference Poisson PINN: independent grid error u_{\rm exact}(x)=\sin(\pi x);\quad -u_{xx}=\pi^2\sin(\pi x),\quad 0<x<1,\quad u(0)=u(1)=0;\quad u_\theta(x)=x(1-x)\left[b_0+\sum_{j=1}^{16}a_j\tanh(w_jx+b_j)\right];\quad r_i=\frac{-u_{\theta,xx}(x_i)-\pi^2\sin(\pi x_i)}{\pi^2},\quad L=\frac1{64}\sum_{i=1}^{64}r_i^2 Solve dimensionless −uₓₓ=π² sin(πx) on [0,1] with zero Dirichlet data. Use sixteen hidden units, 49 real parameters, seeds 8401–8403, 64 training points and 257 separate evaluation points. This fixed-budget study covers one smooth Poisson problem and three seeds. A small training loss does not establish independent-point accuracy or general PINN training success. Unmet goals remain visible. References and results of execution examples Common execution example 1D Poisson: Dirichlet sine solution and second-order refinement CSV aligns finest-grid x, numerical/analytic values and error. JSON retains all three errors/residuals and adjacent-level orders. The Thomas original report remains unverified in the existing catalog, so no newly verified primary-source claim is added. Saved result / JSON Reference and validation details → Numerical methods Methods explicitly bound to this problem by the common fixed-input execution example. Inspect its input for differences from the figure’s conditions. Train a hard-boundary tanh ansatz with trust-region reflective least squares and an analytic parameter Jacobian. Retain every returned model under the fixed budget. Also solve second-order finite differences with 31, 63 and 127 unknowns using the Thomas algorithm. Methods used by this problem’s execution examples Thomas tridiagonal elimination Method-registry status: Educational example / related code PINNs and neural operators Method-registry status: Educational example / related code Code and execution Common execution example 1D Poisson: Dirichlet sine solution and second-order refinement Use the existing Thomas kernel for −u''=π²sin(πx) with 15/31/63 interior nodes; separately check analytic sin(πx), a recomputed discrete residual and halving-grid refinement. Conditions, commands and validation scope Assumptions Constant-coefficient three-point differences on a uniform mesh. Inputs fix domain, boundaries, forcing, grids and solver. The SPD tridiagonal system suits unpivoted Thomas; this does not validate arbitrary tridiagonal matrices.
